_doc: Coefficients of the soil rules (sim/geography/soil_derivation.py, soil_water_balance.py; Complaint 543).

entries.unit: degrees C, daily maximum less minimum
entries.source: Hargreaves evaporation needs the daily range (FAO-56 eq 52, Allen et al. 1998, opened: fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e07.htm); the map has monthly means only, so one land range stands in; no source found for the value
entries.why: Scales every tile's evaporation by its square root; a daily range layer replaces it.

entries.source: Equal to agriculture.ARD_TILLAGE_CAPACITY (a test holds them equal): the arable share is the ground the ard of the old table's era ploughed, so a toolkit with this capacity opens exactly the arable share, a heavier one opens heavy ground beyond it and a lighter one less
entries.why: Anchor of the arable share's tillage: heavy-plough gains and hoe losses are measured against it.

entries.source: The largest arable share the old climate table gave any class (Mediterranean and humid subtropical, tools/generate_geography_tiles.py history); no land-cover source opened
entries.why: Share of a tile with enough moisture and warmth that is not rock, marsh, settlement or pasture; a land-cover layer replaces it.

entries.source: UNEP aridity index classes (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aridity_index, opened): hyperarid below 0.05, arid 0.05 to 0.20
entries.why: Below it no rainfed crop is possible (river-watered strips are in crop_site).

entries.source: UNEP class boundary between semi-arid (0.20 to 0.50) and dry subhumid (0.50 to 0.65) (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aridity_index, opened); taking it as the point where rainfed grain is no longer water-limited is mine
entries.why: Above it dryness no longer cuts the arable share.

entries.unit: months at or above the growth threshold
entries.source: No source found
entries.why: Fewer warm months than this and no crop ripens, so the tile has no arable ground.

entries.unit: months at or above the growth threshold
entries.source: No source found; set so boreal cropland falls to about three fifths of temperate
entries.why: Months of warmth for the full arable share; between the least and this the share rises in a straight line.

entries.source: Steppe black earth forms where rain nearly balances evaporation (Jenny 1941, Factors of Soil Formation; recalled, not opened)
entries.why: Aridity index of the deepest humus.

entries.unit: natural-log units of the aridity index
entries.source: No source found; set so hot desert falls to about half the optimum
entries.why: How fast humus, and so fertility, falls with dryness or excess rain.

entries.source: No source found; hot soils mineralise and leach faster (Brady and Weil, not opened)
entries.why: Mean temperature where leaching of a wet soil starts.

entries.source: No source found
entries.why: Mean temperature where a wet soil leaches fully.

entries.source: UNEP dry subhumid lower bound (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aridity_index, opened): from here rain leaves a surplus over the growing season on hot ground; taking it as the leaching onset is mine
entries.why: Rain over evaporation where drainage through the soil begins.

entries.source: No source found
entries.why: Rain over evaporation where drainage is strongest.

entries.source: No source found; set so rainforest soil falls below the Mediterranean reference
entries.why: Fertility lost on hot soil with rain far beyond evaporation.

entries.source: The old tundra anchor, sim/world/agriculture.py ARCTIC_QUALITY_MULTIPLIER; a parcel with no soil still has a positive multiplier
entries.why: Lowest fertility any tile reports, so no parcel divides by zero.

entries.source: No source found
entries.why: Fertility of ground with no growing season at all, which then yields nothing through the temperature suitability.

entries.source: No source found; heavy clay lowlands of north-west Europe needed the heavy wheeled plough (historical accounts, not opened)
entries.why: Largest share of arable ground that is heavy clay, on flat wet land; a soil texture layer replaces it.

entries.source: No source found
entries.why: Ruggedness above which no fine sediment collects.

entries.source: No source found
entries.why: Rain over evaporation where heavy soil starts to form.

entries.source: No source found
entries.why: Rain over evaporation where the heavy share reaches its ceiling.
